title: Decode: MegaMoE NVFP4 EP32 + shared-expert overlap
shape: D3-32 r24: 96 requests / DP rank (384 verify rows), SP shard = 96 MoE tokens per GPU, 28 local experts, top-16, L~135K, k=3
basis: baseline: gap512 EP16 in-step profile B92 (r23) moved to EP32 by the 8-node step delta (coordinator seed). Per-layer reference: moe_ep32 FI a368c5f66 standalone EP32 NVFP4 T64/T128 = 62.8/69.1 us vs model ach 36.1/37.8 us
gap_analysis: Per layer at EP32 NVFP4 (FI a368c5f66 standalone, Hecate): T1 50.4 us vs ach 17.3 (2.9x), T32 60.2 vs 35.2 (1.71x), T~96 ~66 vs ~37 (1.8x). A fixed per-call chain of ~50 us (same at every EP and both quants) dominates decode; the weight stream itself is a minority of the time. In tree today decode D3-32 runs the vendored DeepGEMM fp8_fp4 MegaMoE (no NVFP4 W4A4 EP32 backend exists), and the shared-expert GEMMs run serially after it (the side-stream overlap only exists on the kimi_k3_mega_moe path, which has no EP32 knobs). Next: 1-GPU (28 experts) and EP4 (112 experts) emulation of the EP32 per-GPU shape with FI a368c5f66 on WS_PYTHONPATH, torch-profiler kernel split + stamp buffer for the fixed chain.
inefficiencies: MEASURED (Hecate moe_ep32): fixed per-call chain ~50 us at T1 vs model 17 us; same at EP16/28/32 and for MX/NVFP4
In-tree decode uses vendored DeepGEMM fp8_fp4 MegaMoE (no NVFP4 W4A4 at EP32 in any tree)

HYPOTHESIS: router/landing + phase-interleave scheduler polling + combine barrier dominate the fixed chain (to be measured with the stamp buffer)
